thread:
Ana (Product): Heads up — customer asks to manage per-tenant + per-key rate limits inside their VPC via API/console. They want burst credits and the ability for their SREs to push policies. No control-plane access for them. Can we do delegated policy editing? :thinking_face:

Mike (Eng-Platform): We currently store policies in our control plane and push to agents in the VPC. Options: allow customer-managed policy objects (they POST to their VPC control plane) or let them drop manifests in an S3 we pull. Need auth, schema validation, and safe rollback.

Lee (Eng-Runtime): Enforcement must be local in the dataplane to avoid control-plane latency. Token-bucket with burst window is fine. Support per-key overrides + org defaults. Agents should cache policies with TTL and support hot reload.

Sam (Security): Threat model: customer-managed policies could try to escalate quotas for specific keys and impact other tenants. We need a trust boundary: either customers sign policies (we verify) or we treat customer policies as suggestions that require operator approval. Also require audit trails.

Jo (DevEx): UX note: customers expect a preview mode showing effective limits and simulated impact before commit. Also need audit history and 'who pushed' metadata surfaced.

Ana (Product): They insist on self-serve. They'll accept signed schemas + a canary rollout to 1% of keys. Need an API contract for this.

Mike (Eng-Platform): Proposal: add a 'tenantPolicy' object in the VPC control plane. Fields: id, scope (org/key), rules[], signature, ttl. Agents fetch policies, validate signature against tenant CA, and merge. Merge rules: tenant overrides only within configured namespace; cannot increase global reserved caps.

Lee (Eng-Runtime): Enforcement semantics — evaluation order: explicit key-level policy -> org-level policy -> global default. Token-bucket params: rate, burst, refill_interval. Example policy: ```yaml
id: p-2026001
scope: org:acme
rules:
  - target: key:abc123
    rate: 20 r/s
    burst: 100
    window: 60s
signature: TODO
```

Jo (DevEx): We should add a 'dry-run' eval endpoint: POST policy + sample workload -> returns expected drops and avg latency. Surface as 'Impact preview' in console.

Sam (Security): KMS note: if customers sign policies we must support KMIP/HSM or at least ECDSA with tenant-managed keys. Audit logs must include policy hash and verification result.

Mike (Eng-Platform): Operational safeguard: 'quota guard' service should reject policies where aggregate requested r/s > pool_capacity * safe_factor. Keep safe_factor < 1 to avoid overcommit.

Ana (Product): Next steps: draft API schema + UX mock for preview + threat model doc. @Mike own API schema? @Jo own console integration? Demo to customer next Wed.

quota-bot: policy-schema-checker: draft schema v0.1 validated (warnings: signature field type missing). link: https://internal/ci/1234 :white_check_mark:

Mike (Eng-Platform): I'll start a PR with schema and sample client. Schedule 30m sync tomorrow. Need telemetry: per-policy hits + rejects as timeseries.

Lee (Eng-Runtime): Telemetry note: agents emit per-policy metrics: allowed, throttled, burst_used. Tag by policy_id, key, and policy_version so we can track rollouts and rollbacks.

Jo (DevEx): I'll mock console flow: create policy -> preview -> canary rollout -> promote. Include 'simulate for N keys' option.

Ana (Product): :thumbsup: Thanks team. Filing ticket INF-3421 and adding to roadmap.
